cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Say You Missed Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. You're selling the sofa but keeping my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody offered anything for it. Have you brought its cushion back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. If someone offered twenty pounds, would you still keep it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I like pretending you're about to sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll admit I sleep with the cushion. Could you take the price sticker off before I sit?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks about the chair and A3 price probes attachment before A5 disclosure, but the actual questions are ordinary testing rather than high-status approval beyond prefixes.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 no offer explains keeping chair; A3 tests a hypothetical offer; B4 admits longing, causing A5 cushion confession.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers a practical explanation and asks for the cushion; B4 finally names attachment, giving A a real first admission.

heightening.evidence: B4 imagined presence allows A5 to admit a parallel attachment and propose actually sitting.

specificity.evidence: A1 selling furniture and B2 missing cushion establish objects; A5 price sticker fits a chair previously offered for sale.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 cushion sleeping and sticker removal are earned by chair attachment, though stock rank wording is awkward.
